missing_information_behavior: Check current vitamin C intake and products; do not add a supplement automatically if dietary and existing supplemental intake are adequate.
safety_exclusions: Do not frame vitamin C supplementation as a way to offset smoking harms.
Do not recommend high-dose vitamin C to prevent smoking-related disease.
Smoking cessation remains the key health intervention.
professional_escalation_conditions: Respiratory symptoms, chronic disease, pregnancy or high-dose supplement use.
History of kidney stones or iron overload requires additional review.
population_and_context: Adults who smoke; U.S. dietary reference guidance sets higher vitamin C intake for smokers, but smoking status alone does not establish deficiency or a need for high-dose supplements.
dose_constraints: Use jurisdiction-appropriate dietary reference values; no individualized supplemental dose from this rule.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Vitamin C fact sheet describes higher reference intake for smokers; it does not establish that supplementation neutralizes tobacco-related risk. This justification remains draft pending source passage verification, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional review.
